correctness.rationale: Unique-path probability gives the exact expected outbreak count; polynomial endpoint factorization is elementary. Exact finite Prüfer census covers all labelled n-vertex trees, n=2..7 (up to 16,807 at n=7), with canonical unlabelled representatives and all unordered sources. Rational Sturm isolation proves zero interior crossing for n<=6 and exactly three reversing representative pairs, in two marked-edge classes, at n=7. Independent explicit witness formulas and exhaustive 64-edge-subset expectations confirm the exact two crossing thresholds. Separate NetworkX/SymPy enumeration agrees with the counts. No infinite classification is inferred.

originality.rationale: Gordon and Jager (2009/2010) already prove unrestricted qualitative reversals by realization of arbitrary endpoint-vanishing integer polynomials (Lemma 2.4 and Proposition 2.5). That strong prior does not determine the first possible tree order or classify all source pairs there. New exact Prüfer/Sturm census establishes a sharp seven-node obstruction and the two minimal marked-edge orbits. Eisenstat et al. (2008) develop the underlying polynomial, not the finite cutoff. Accessible prior claims and specialized literature searches produced no matching minimum-seven theorem; older inaccessible full text is a real priority risk and independent audit remains outstanding.

value.rationale: The number of hosts necessary for transmissibility to reverse two specified seed sites’ expected outbreak-size ordering is a natural structural boundary in independent-transmission epidemic networks. Seven is the exact onset, uniquely realized in two branching geometries; high-transmission reach overturns the small-p degree preference at exact distinct thresholds. The complete minimal classification is not an arbitrary numerical slice and informs when structural rankings can fail. Qualitative crossing existence was already known and is excluded from the new claim.
